overview: Two double-membraned, semi-autonomous organelles with their own DNA, each central to one half of the energy cycle of life.
genZNote: Mitochondria burn the fuel. Chloroplasts make it.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The "powerhouse of the cell" — converts chemical energy in food into ATP via aerobic respiration.
aspects.valueB: The site of photosynthesis in plant/algal cells — converts light energy into chemical energy stored as glucose.

aspects.label: Primary Process
aspects.valueA: Cellular respiration: oxidative phosphorylation and the citric acid (Krebs) cycle.
aspects.valueB: Photosynthesis: light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle.

aspects.label: Pigment
aspects.valueB: Contains chlorophyll, giving chloroplasts (and plants) their green color.

aspects.label: Energy Conversion
aspects.valueA: Converts chemical energy (glucose/fatty acids + O2) into ATP, releasing CO2 and water.
aspects.valueB: Converts light energy into chemical energy (glucose), releasing O2 as a byproduct.

aspects.label: Occurrence
aspects.valueA: Present in nearly all eukaryotic cells (plant and animal).
aspects.valueB: Present only in plant cells and algae, absent in animal cells and fungi.

aspects.label: Own DNA / Endosymbiotic Origin
aspects.valueA: Contains its own circular DNA and ribosomes; believed to have originated from an engulfed aerobic bacterium.
aspects.valueB: Contains its own circular DNA and ribosomes; believed to have originated from an engulfed photosynthetic cyanobacterium.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Produces ATP via respiration; found in animal and plant cells.
aspects.valueB: Produces glucose via photosynthesis; found only in plant/algal cells.

overlay.memoryTrick: "Mitochondria: respiration, releases CO2. Chloroplast: photosynthesis, releases O2."
